data.gender_notes: Kamakshi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Desire or Longing for the Divine
data.long_meaning: Kamakshi is a form of the goddess Parvati, who is known to fulfill the deepest desires of her devotees. Her name is derived from 'Kama' (desire) and 'Kshi' (fulfillment). She is often depicted with a lotus in her hand, symbolizing the fulfillment of spiritual desires. The name Kamakshi carries the meaning “Desire or Longing for the Divine” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kamakshi usually hope their child will grow to embody desire or longing for the divine and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Kamakshi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire or Longing for the Divine.”

historical_references.reference: Kamakshi is a form of the Hindu goddess Parvati, who is often depicted with lotus flowers in her hands and a third eye on her forehead. This form is particularly popular in Tamil Nadu, South India. The name 'Kamakshi' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kama' meaning desire and 'Ishwari' meaning Goddess. Kamakshi is believed to be the embodiment of desire and love in the universe.

Another interpretation of the name 'Kamakshi' is that it refers to the goddess as the one who fulfills desire. This form of the goddess is believed to have originated in the Chola period (9th to 13th century) and is particularly associated with the temple town of Kancipuram in Tamil Nadu. The goddess is depicted with a lotus in her hand, symbolizing purity and detachment, and with a third eye, representing her power to see and fulfill desires.
